questions_and_answers.question_text: What does -dào mean with verbs of perception?
What do Běijīng speakers prefer in many contexts?
What pattern can biàn be used in?
Give the three meanings of -dào you have now seen.

answers.answer_text: (1) "To successfully reach/obtain/find," (2) "about" with verbs of speech, and (3) successful perceiving with verbs of the senses.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Please translate this article into Japanese."

answers.answer_text: Qǐng ni bǎ zhèipiān wénzhāng fānyìchéng Rìwén.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "This child has already grown into an adult."

answers.answer_text: Zhèige háizi yǐjing zhǎngchéng dàren le.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "He has become a lot healthier since last year."

answers.answer_text: Cóng qùnián dào xiànzài, tā biànde jiànkāngduō le.

articles.text:
10. A: Nǐ zhèicì huí guó kàndào nǐ  Did you see the people in your hometown
       lǎojiāde rén le ma?           on this visit back to your country?
    B: Kàndào le. Tāmen shēnghuóde  Yes, they're living pretty well, and my
       bú cuò, wǒ lǎojiā yě          hometown has become quite a bustling
       biànchéng yíge hěn rènàode    place.
       dìfangr le.

Notes on No. 10

kàndào: "to see, to perceive by sight." This is another example of the ending -dào used as part of a compound verb of result. You have now seen -dào meaning (1) "to successfully reach/obtain/find" and (2) "about." With VERBS OF PERCEPTION, the meaning of -dào can be thought of as "successfully reach BY MEANS OF THE SENSES," or "to successfully perceive." Another instance is tīngdào, "to hear."

Běijīng speakers prefer kànjian and tīngjian in many contexts, but kàndào and tīngdào are used by all speakers of Standard Chinese.

biàn: "to change, to become different, to transform, to alter"

Zhèige rén zhēnde biàn le,       This fellow has really changed, he
yǐqián tā bú shi zhèiyàngrde.    wasn't this way before.
Jǐnián bú jiàn, tā yǐjing biàn   I hadn't seen him for a few years; he
lǎo le.                          had aged a lot.

You can also use biàn in the pattern biàn-de-STATE VERB:

Cóng qùnián dào xiànzài, tā      He has become a lot healthier since
biànde jiànkāngduō le.           last year.

-chéng: "become," "into." This is used with a number of verbs to form a compound: gǎichéng, "to change (one thing) into (another)"; fānyìchéng, "to translate into"; zuòchéng, "to make into"; zhǎngchéng, "to grow into."

Qǐng ni bǎ zhèipiān wénzhāng     Please translate this article into
fānyìchéng Rìwén.                Japanese.
Zhèige háizi yǐjing zhǎngchéng   This child has already grown into an
dàren le.                        adult.
